testName: Air Brakes Test #2 25 Questions • Passing Score 20

questions.question: What type of brakes do most newer heavy-duty trucks have?
questions.correctAnswerText: Dual air brakes
questions.explanation: Most newer heavy-duty trucks use dual air brake systems. This system has two separate air brake systems that share one set of brake controls.

questions.question: What does the application pressure gauge show?

options.text: How much air pressure is being applied to the brakes.
The temperature of air in the braking system.
The pressure of air from the compressor.
How many times the brakes have been used.

questions.correctAnswerText: How much air pressure is being applied to the brakes.
questions.explanation: The application pressure gauge shows how much air pressure is being applied to the brakes. Not all air brake systems have this gauge.

questions.question: Which item is NOT part of an air brake system?
questions.correctAnswerText: Air filter
questions.explanation: Air brake systems include an air compressor, air tanks, gauges, a low air pressure warning, a brake pedal, foundation brakes, spring brakes, and parking brake controls. An air filter is not part of the air brake system.

questions.question: While driving, what keeps spring brakes in place?
questions.correctAnswerText: Air pressure.
questions.explanation: Air pressure keeps spring brakes in place while driving. If air pressure drops too low, the springs will activate the brakes.

questions.question: What does an application pressure gauge show?

options.text: How much air pressure is being applied to the brakes.
How much air pressure is available.
How much air pressure is needed to stop the vehicle.

questions.correctAnswerText: How much air pressure is being applied to the brakes.
questions.explanation: The application pressure gauge shows how much air pressure is being applied to the brakes. It helps drivers know if their brakes are beginning to fade.

questions.question: What can happen if you don't drain air tanks?

options.text: Water can freeze and cause brake failure.
Too much air collects in the tanks.

questions.correctAnswerText: Water can freeze and cause brake failure.
questions.explanation: Air tanks must be drained regularly to remove water and compressor oil. If water is left in the tanks, it can freeze in cold weather and cause the brakes to fail.

questions.question: What prevents air from escaping if the air compressor leaks?
questions.correctAnswerText: One-way check valve
questions.explanation: A one-way check valve is installed between the air compressor and the first air tank. It stops air from escaping if the compressor leaks.

questions.question: When parked on a flat surface, what should you do?

options.text: Use wheel chocks to prevent your vehicle from moving.
Use wheel chocks only after you apply the parking brake.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use wheel chocks to prevent your vehicle from moving.
questions.explanation: Always use wheel chocks when parking on a flat surface. This prevents the trailer from moving, especially if the vehicle does not have spring brakes.

questions.question: In a dual parking control valve system, if spring brakes engage due to lost air pressure, what can you do?

options.text: A separate air tank can release the spring brakes temporarily.
You can drive normally using the spring brakes.
The air tanks refill automatically to a safe pressure.

questions.correctAnswerText: A separate air tank can release the spring brakes temporarily.
questions.explanation: In a dual parking control valve system, a separate air tank can temporarily release the spring brakes if they engage. By pushing the correct control, you can release the brakes for a short time in an emergency to move the vehicle.

questions.question: If ABS is on only one axle, what happens?

options.text: You still have more braking control than without ABS.
It slows the vehicle but cannot stop it.

questions.correctAnswerText: You still have more braking control than without ABS.
questions.explanation: If your vehicle has ABS on only one axle or only the tractor or trailer, you still have better braking control than a vehicle without ABS. Brake normally as usual.

questions.question: If your tractor has ABS but your trailer does not, what happens to the ABS?

options.text: It will still help you steer better.
It will make jackknifing more likely.
It will let others see when you brake.

questions.correctAnswerText: It will still help you steer better.
questions.explanation: When a tractor has ABS but the trailer does not, the ABS still helps the driver control steering. Watch the trailer and ease off the brakes if it starts to swing out.

questions.question: In a vehicle with dual air brakes, a leak in one system ____ the second system.
questions.correctAnswerText: May not affect
questions.explanation: A dual air brake system has two separate systems. A leak in one system may not affect the other.

questions.question: What type of force must emergency brakes use?
questions.correctAnswerText: Mechanical
questions.explanation: Air pressure can leak away over time. Emergency brakes in an air brake system must use mechanical force to hold the brakes on.

questions.question: What was the purpose of front brake limiting valves?

options.text: To stop the front tires from skidding.
To stop the front tires from overheating.

questions.correctAnswerText: To stop the front tires from skidding.
questions.explanation: Some older vehicles have front brake limiting valves. These were designed to prevent front wheels from skidding. Research showed these devices are not needed, so they should be left in the normal position.

questions.question: What can happen if you use the parking brake in very wet, freezing weather?

options.text: The brakes may freeze and lock the vehicle.
The brakes may release by themselves.

questions.correctAnswerText: The brakes may freeze and lock the vehicle.
questions.explanation: Using the parking brake in very wet, freezing weather can cause the brakes to freeze. This will prevent the vehicle from moving.

questions.question: How many air storage tanks does an air brake system have?
questions.correctAnswerText: The number varies.
questions.explanation: Air storage tanks hold compressed air. The number and size of tanks in an air brake system varies by vehicle.

questions.question: In a dual air brake system, air pressure should build from 85 to 100 psi in ____ seconds.
questions.explanation: When checking a dual air brake system, wait for air pressure to build from 85 to 100 psi in both the primary and secondary systems. This should take about 45 seconds.

questions.question: What happens if brake pads rub against brake drums and create too much heat?

options.text: The brakes will become more sensitive.
The air compressor will turn on to cool the brakes.

questions.correctAnswerText: The brakes may stop working.
questions.explanation: Brakes heat up when used. If they overheat, they become less effective and may stop working completely. This is called brake fade.

questions.question: If an air compressor has a belt, it should be checked to make sure it is:
questions.correctAnswerText: Properly tight.
questions.explanation: Check the air compressor belt before each trip. Make sure it is tight and in good condition.

questions.question: If the low pressure warning light comes on while driving, what should you do?

options.text: Safely exit the road and park as soon as possible.
Turn on hazard lights and keep driving.

questions.correctAnswerText: Safely exit the road and park as soon as possible.
questions.explanation: When the low pressure warning light comes on, safely exit the road and park your vehicle right away. If air pressure gets too low, your brakes will not work well enough to stop safely.

questions.question: What do ABS brakes do?

options.text: Stop your wheels from locking up.
Stop your vehicle from speeding up on hills.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop your wheels from locking up.
questions.explanation: ABS (Anti-Lock Braking System) stops your wheels from locking up when you brake hard on slippery surfaces.

questions.question: When driving a vehicle with dual air brakes, what should you do first?

options.text: Let the vehicle warm up to get fuel to the engine.
Let the air compressor build up at least 100 psi pressure in both systems before driving.
Start driving right after the engine starts.

questions.correctAnswerText: Let the air compressor build up at least 100 psi pressure in both systems before driving.
questions.explanation: Before driving a vehicle with dual air brakes, wait for the air compressor to build up at least 100 psi pressure in both the primary and secondary systems. Check the air pressure gauges to monitor the levels.

questions.question: In a dual air brake system, how are the air tanks arranged?

options.text: Both systems share the same air tanks.
Each system has its own separate air tanks.
You choose which system's tanks to use.

questions.correctAnswerText: Each system has its own separate air tanks.
questions.explanation: A dual air brake system has two separate brake systems. They share brake controls, but each system has its own tanks, hoses, and lines.

questions.question: What should control the emergency brake?
questions.correctAnswerText: Mechanical force.
questions.explanation: All trucks, truck tractors, and buses must have emergency and parking brakes controlled by mechanical force. Air pressure can leak away, so these brakes must be held by mechanical force.

questions.question: If the spring brakes are on, what should you do?

options.text: Do not press the brake pedal.

questions.correctAnswerText: Do not press the brake pedal.
questions.explanation: Do not press the brake pedal when spring brakes are on. This can damage the brakes by forcing springs and air pressure to work together.
